A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite revisions to the theory and the addition of Appendix F.

before.justification: V2 reports original Gaussian/RRF experiments and neural-network measurements of classification accuracy, OOD detection and Neural Collapse in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds depth-scaling results in Appendix F, Table 4 and Figures 23–24.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the analyzed classifier from fitting noisy probabilities using X_T^+y to fitting noisy logits using X_T^+z, moving Gaussian noise inside the activation. This changes the theoretical estimator's training objective; the NC1 regime-selection criterion and empirical OOD detector algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian toy setting, CIFAR-10/100 classification tasks and OOD datasets: CIFAR-10/100, SUN, Places365, ImageNet-O, Textures and iNaturalist. The added depth experiments change model configurations within existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.7 and Table 1 add the accuracy ratio Acc_o/u as a comparison indicator against the proposed NC1 criterion. The evaluated OOD detector set is retained; Table 4's ReAct label corresponds to the existing Energy+ReAct configuration described in Appendix B.1.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a controlled depth sweep at fixed width k=10, supplementing the existing width sweeps. Section 5.7 adds accuracy-ratio evaluation, and Section 4.1 revises the documented OOD-risk metric by removing its noisy reference and binary affine rescaling. Existing risk plots are retained, so recomputation under the revised definition is not established.

E4.justification: The new Appendix F investigates whether double descent and the NC1 relationship persist when complexity increases through depth rather than width. Section 5.7 additionally compares NC1 with accuracy as an indicator of OOD performance. These extend the questions tested beyond the retained noise and representation analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five experiments with different random seeds in Section 5.2 and report standard deviations and uncertainty bands. The added results follow the existing reporting practice; no increased run count or new statistical testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V3 adds depth-dependent AUC and risk curves, accuracy ratios in Table 1, and tabulated NC1 levels in Table 3. New Table 4 reports, for example, Softmax SUN AUCs of 72.45±0.99 underparameterized and 69.23±2.66 overparameterized. The earlier AUC table entries and figure curves are retained; the additions do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 4 revises the response model and risk definitions, strengthens the activation assumption, and replaces covariance nonsingularity with a subspace condition. Theorems 1–2 now assert bounds using weight-independent constants, and Appendix A substantially revises their proofs and lemmas. The underparameterized coefficient changes from n/(n-p-1) to p/(n-p-1).

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contributions retain their central claims. Section 5.7 adds a claimed first demonstration of depth-wise double descent, and the conclusion removes the earlier restriction of the study to model width.

C2.justification: V3 interprets NC1 as a better indicator of OOD performance than the accuracy ratio. Appendix F explains the comparable depth-regime performance through the lack of improved feature collapse, emphasizes differences between scaling depth and width, and adds qualifications about optimization instability and slower convergence at large depths.

D1.justification: V3 adds an explicit code hyperlink beside the abstract and documents construction rules for the depth experiments, including balanced layer additions and MaxPooling substitutions for shallow models. The existing architecture and hyperparameter descriptions are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the linked resource's availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds Couillet and Liao's Random Matrix Methods for Machine Learning and removes Fort et al. (2021), replacing its architectural discussion citation with the already-cited Tripuraneni work. It also positions the depth results as a first demonstration. Most remaining reference changes concern metadata or duplicate entries.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the theoretical setup, reorganizes Appendix A around risk proofs and shared lemmas, and adds Appendix F while retaining the main section sequence. It also corrects cross-references and terminology and changes the author footnote from corresponding authorship to equal contribution.

P2.justification: V3 enlarges Table 1 and incorporates accuracy-ratio entries, adds Tables 3–4 and Figures 23–24, and adjusts captions and placement. Existing Figures 1–22 retain their plotted content. The principal visual improvements and additions are localized.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful checks of whether the width-based findings extend to depth and whether NC1 is more informative than accuracy. The enlarged Table 1 and code link improve usability. These gains are limited: the theoretical rewrite still claims an infinite peak for bounded probability risks, and Appendix F.1's depth example ends at 40 while Figures 23–24 extend beyond 120. The revision strengthens empirical examination and presentation without resolving the central theoretical validity issue.
